name: glitch-cut
title: Glitch Cut
description: A hard cut torn into displaced horizontal slices with red/blue channel split and corrupted blocks that leak the other scene; each band hands over at its own moment. Runs its WebGL shader over two built-in panels (a stat and a bar chart, then a render queue; text and colours from variables), not over the host's scenes: 45 frames of the first panel, a 12-frame transition, then the second panel. To use it between your own scenes, copy the shader into your composition and feed it your two frames as textures.
useWhen: The cut lands in a tech or developer-facing demo and should read as a deliberate broadcast artifact instead of a smooth blend.
The rhythm is fast: it holds up at 8 to 14 frames, where softer presentations read as sluggish.
The two scenes are visually unrelated and the hard cut between them needs an excuse.
avoidWhen: Only a headline should glitch while the scene around it stays intact: use rgb-glitch-text.
The demo needs a calm, general-purpose cut: use zoom-blur.
author: Remocn

variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small heading above the list in the sample scene.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).

variables.label: Intensity
variables.description: How far slices and blocks are displaced.

variables.label: Slices
variables.description: Number of horizontal bands that can tear.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Slices and blocks are coarse; 0.75 matches 1 in the stills.
